text.p: HealthCare Compare Corp, which provides medical cost management services to employers, said it is comfortable with analysts estimates of earnings per share of $2.25 for the 1996 year.
"We're comfortable with analysts estimates right in the neighborhood of $2.25," chief financial officer Joseph Whitters told a Dain Bosworth health care conference here.
He also estimated 1996 revenues at about $250 million. "We'll have business this year right around a quarter of a billion dollars in revenues," Whitters said.
In 1995, HealthCare Compare earned $1.89 on total revenues of $214.3 million.

Following the meeting, Whitters told Reuters that the rate of growth in fee schedule revenues would slow. "The 50 percent growth in fee service revenues in the first half is going to be hard to maintain," he said.
"For the last half of the year, we will be up somewhere in the neighborhood of 30 to 40 percent (growth)," he said.
In 1997 and beyond, fee schedule revenue growth would be about 20 percent annually, he said.

HealthCare Compare recently entered the risk business and he said he expects revenues to increase dramatically over the next three years. "As we finish this year, the risk business will be around $7 to $8 million in premium dollars. Next year it will be around $15 to $20 million. Two years from now we should be looking at revenues north of $50 million," he said.
Whitters said that mid-sized employers, that is those with 500 to 5,000 employees, would be the target market for the company's risk product offering.
